test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 16 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: On which date was World Malaria Day 2025 observed with the theme Malaria Ends with Us: Reinvest, Reimagine, Reignite?
solution:
The correct answer is __**April 25**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Malaria Day** is an international observance commemorated every year on **April 25** to recognize global efforts to control malaria.
 
• The theme for **World Malaria Day 2025** is "**Malaria Ends with Us: Reinvest, Reimagine, Reignite**." This theme calls for a renewed commitment to funding, innovative strategies, and a reinvigorated spirit to eliminate the disease.
 
• The day was established by the **World Health Assembly** at its **60th session** in **May 2007**. It was designed to provide education and understanding of malaria and spread information on year-long intensified implementation of national malaria-control strategies.
 
• Before **World Malaria Day**, **Africa Malaria Day** was observed on the same date, starting in **2001**, following the historic **Abuja Declaration** by **44** malaria-endemic countries.
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** uses this platform to highlight the need for continued investment and sustained political commitment for malaria prevention and control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Disease Profile**: **Malaria** is a life-threatening disease caused by **Plasmodium parasites** that are transmitted to people through the bites of infected female **Anopheles mosquitoes**. Among the five parasite species that cause malaria in humans, **P. falciparum** and **P. vivax** pose the greatest threat.
 
• **Prevention and Treatment**: Key interventions include the use of **Long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs)**, **Indoor residual spraying (IRS)**, and **Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT)** for treatment.
 
• **Vaccine Development**: A major milestone was reached with the recommendation of the **RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix)** vaccine in **October 2021** and the **R21/Matrix-M** vaccine in **2023** for children living in regions with moderate to high malaria transmission.
 
• **Global Burden**: According to the **World Malaria Report**, the **WHO African Region** carries a disproportionately high share of the global malaria burden, accounting for approximately **94%** of cases and **95%** of deaths globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SDG Target**: The **United Nations** Sustainable Development Goal **(SDG) 3.3** aims to end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, **malaria**, and neglected tropical diseases by the **year 2030**.
 
• **Elimination Certification**: The **WHO** grants a "**Malaria-Free Certification**" to countries that have demonstrated, beyond a reasonable doubt, that the chain of indigenous transmission has been interrupted nationwide for at least the consecutive **last 3 years**.
 
• **Recent Successes**: In **2023**, **Azerbaijan** and **Tajikistan** were certified malaria-free, followed by **Cabo Verde** in early **2024**, showcasing that elimination is achievable with persistent effort.
 
• **Global Technical Strategy**: The **WHO Global Technical Strategy for Malaria 2016–2030** aims to reduce malaria case incidence and mortality rates by at least **90%** by **2030** compared to **2015** levels.
